issue.title: Source maps are using deprecated //@ instead of //#

repository.name: webpack
repository.description: A bundler for javascript and friends. Packs many modules into a few bundled assets. Code Splitting allows for loading parts of the application on demand. Through "loaders", modules can be CommonJs, AMD, ES6 modules, CSS, Images, JSON, Coffeescript, LESS, ... and your custom stuff.

issue.body:
Firefox gave me these deprecated warnings and I think that they are coming from source map related code.

```
SyntaxError: Using //@ to indicate sourceURL pragmas is deprecated. Use //# instead
Use of getPreventDefault() is deprecated.  Use defaultPrevented instead.
```

Should it be changed?

body: This bug just showed up in my Canary again after upgrading

Same as @trueter , `inline-eval-cheap-source-map`.
@trueter do you know which setting I should use in the mean time to prevent these errors? I disabled all sourcemaps yesterday because I was in a hurry but I need them back..

@vkammerer Sorry, no idea. As far as I see it two things are possible here:
1) Since it's only on Canary and not happening in stable Chrome it might be an issue with Canary we can't influence. 
2) There's been an issue with the devtool and Canary is reporting it while stable Chrome is not. 

Because it was apparently reporting back in 2013 and I don't see why they would remove that warning, I guess 1) is more likely.

issue.body: Am I the only one seeing this in chrome canary 51? `'//@ sourceURL' and '//@ sourceMappingURL' are deprecated, please use '//# sourceURL=' and '//# sourceMappingURL=' instead.` https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2013/06/sourceMappingURL-and-sourceURL-syntax-changed

body: seeing this as well. my devtool setting ``` json devtool: ( process.env.DEBUG ? 'eval-source-map' : 'cheap-module-eval-source-map'), ```
My quick fix for the moment is to use 'cheap-source-map'
I'm also getting this on Chrome Dev - 50.0.2657.0 dev (64-bit)
Also seeing this using 'eval-source-map', changing it to '#eval-source-map' fixes it for now

[According to the docs](http://webpack.github.io/docs/configuration.html#devtool) `#` is the default now:

> Prefixing @, # or #@ will enforce a pragma style. (Defaults to #, recommended)

Seeing it as well, anything I can do?

> `Chrome Version 50.0.2661.26 beta (64-bit)`
@himynameisdave You can switch to `cheap-source-map` for now.
